tag: Episode 51S · The Spring We Chose to Stay
title: The One Who Stays

beats.t: Yeoni's finger touched the moonlit World Tree card. The entire square drew a light breath, and the cherry-blossom view through the open door quietly receded.
[ Choice complete · Stay in the world of fortune ]
I'll stay. I want to live my next spring where the people I protected are.
Then I stay too. Not a rule. Park Byeongha's choice.
The light from the door settled at their feet. Neo took Yeoni’s hand. It was a human hand, with its name and memories intact.
Yeoni, I'll return. There are debts to face and people to apologize to there.
Repay what you owe. But don’t put off eating or smiling until every debt is settled.
Yes. Beside the repayments, I'll record the meals too.
Yeoni took her apartment key from her pocket, its keychain a flower pig. She laid it on Hanbi's palm.
Water the plant, please. And let Mom in when she comes.
Me? May I really hold the key to your room?
You may. Hands that held a ledger should hold a key well enough.
Hanbi couldn't open her hand for a long time. The hand that had trembled when breaking the ring now trembled around something received.
Yeoni opened the yellow umbrella and placed it in Seo Hanbi's hand. Its shaft, wrapped in three layers of tape, was warm between two worlds.
Wait. Take this to reality. The first line of my new song. No copyright yet, so listen all you want.
I don't know whether letters can cross. Even the Universe won't promise.
I'll write to Mom anyway. Until something reaches her.
Yeoni tore a page from her notebook. Dear Mom. After the first line, she stopped over the second for a long time. Finally she added just one line and folded it.
What did the second line say?
Secret. Mom will understand. She knows my rating habit already.
Yeoni gave the folded letter to Hanbi, into the hand holding her key.
Hanbi smiled, a smile absent from the first spring. Umbrella, key, and letter gathered in one hand, she stood before the cherry-blossom door.
See you in the next rain. I'll tilt the umbrella then.
The door closed. A yellow line lingered in the air, then went out before Yeoni could reach for it.
…It really closed.
She pressed her palm where the door had been. It didn't move. Not yet.
All right. Goodbyes done. Everyone staying, eat first. Save the world then starve, and we'll lose all dignity.
Moka spun his pan. Vegetables and flames bounced to the beat. Smiling, Yeoni set plates on the table.
Your chart's moved to this address. I'll register your residence. There is a fee.
Take Moka's meals as the fee. Do I still have to get up in the morning here?
Seven tomorrow. A fortune world doesn't abolish being late.
Considering undoing my choice.
Everyone laughed. Moonlight fell through the World Tree's leaves. Beneath it, Yeoni called this place home for the first time.
After the farewell, the square was quiet. Where the door had stood lay one scrap of tape fallen from Hanbi's umbrella.
Yeoni tucked it into her notebook. The second line of her letter to Mom came back to her.
If Mom answers, the first line will definitely be about food.
A wager? I bet socks.
Following the grain of the World Tree's roots, Byeongha showed them a small homesite. A waterway in view, the teahouse's moonlight within reach, the ladle a little less audible.
Sounds like you're calling my ladle noise. Expect a giant cookware set as your wedding gift.
We haven't discussed marriage! We're only looking at a homesite!
I have, in my mind. I'll say it aloud after the house is built.
Yeoni’s ears reddened. Becoming human again hadn’t made her any better at hiding her feelings. Moka lowered his microphone and grinned like an otter with teasing material for life.
As night deepened, news arrived from the islands they had crossed together. The eclipse had retreated. Stopped festivals resumed. Forgotten names found their owners one by one.
You already have work to do here, Yeoni. After rescue ends, recovery remains.
I can't do that alone. We'll do it together. Being the main character doesn't mean I plan to carry the whole world.
At day's end, Yeoni leaned against a World Tree root. No finished home, no settled job, no complete plan. But the earth beneath their feet was solid.
Byeongha sat beside her. They said nothing for a long time. His shoulder didn't turn transparent once that night.
Let's try living here from tomorrow. Good days and bad, making them all part of my choice.
She placed a little chair where Hanbi had left. Letters might never arrive. Still, she meant to sit there every evening.
From the next day, instead of listing places to return to, she began listing things to do tomorrow.
Tomorrow I'll clean the teahouse windows. The next day, visit the Island of Companions and mend broken mirrors. After that, we'll choose then.
A practical enough plan. Except I'll clean the windows. When you do it, you only add patterns.
Yeoni argued as usual; Byeongha refused to yield as usual. They ended up cleaning half the window each.
Every evening she sat in the chair. The first day, the second—the place where the door had been stayed quiet.
Neo. What if nothing ever comes?
Then we sit together tomorrow. And the day after.
She leaned her head on his shoulder. No sound came from beyond the vanished door. Still, she knew she'd sit in this chair tomorrow evening too.
[ Twenty-third Door · No incoming messages ]
